newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba Red River flood delay seen raising risks.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba Red River flood delay seen raising risks.

text.p: Cool temperatures and a slow melt on the Manitoba side of the Red River Valley may add to the risk of a record flood and planting delays, officials said.

"If we're looking at a later peak, it's not good news. It doesn't necessarily mean later seeding -- that depends on the weather in May -- but it doesn't look good," Paul Bullock, Canadian Wheat Board director of weather and crop surveillance, said in an interview.
About 275 sq mi (700 sq km) flooded last year when the Red peaked on April 20. This year the Red may peak on April 26 at Winnipeg.
Seeding of spring wheat, barley, durum, canola and flax usually begins May 7 but last year's flood delayed Red River seeding to May 29, provincial and private crop reports said.
Manitoba Natural Resources projected a 90 percent chance of a flood similar to last year's and a 50 percent chance of the worst flood of the century exceeding 400 sq mi (1,000 sq km).
"It's got to stay dry to give us any chance of avoiding a record flood," Manitoba Natural Resources director Larry Whitney said.
The Red River was 23.59 feet above its winter level at the U.S. border Tuesday and should reach 40.59 feet by late April.
A flood level of 40.59 feet would exceed floods recorded in the 1860s, Whitney said.
Environment Canada forecast a storm for Saturday with precipitation expected to total 10 mm (0.4 inch) with below normal temperatures through the week. Normal highs are +10 C (50 F).
"At best, we'll be one or two degrees below normal," Environment Canada meteorologist Clarence Spelchak said.
Winnipeg's high on Tuesday was -3 C (27 F).
"This cool weather's not doing us any favors. Normally you'd like to see a slow melt, but not with all hell breaking loose upstream," Whitney said.
"The timing of our melt compared to when the river starts to crest at the border and the American water gets here is going to be critical," Whitney added.
Delayed cresting of the river also compounds the risk of higher and prolonged flooding due to increasing precipitation amounts, the CWB's Bullock said.
Normal precipitation for Winnipeg for the month of April is 36 mm (1.4 inches) but in May it is 60 mm (2.4 inches), he said.
